purpose: Machine-readable context-routing layer. Given a task class, tells an agent which documents and code areas are required, optional, likely to own the change, and off-limits, WITHOUT recursively reading the repository. This file routes to context; it does not restate context. docs/current-state.md is authoritative for active state, docs/findings/index.json is authoritative for which findings document is current, and docs/agent/agent-contract.md is authoritative for process/evidence rules. This file must never duplicate volatile values (counts, accuracy, current commit, open hypotheses) from those sources -- see 'entries[].path' for where the current value lives.
how_to_use: 1. Classify the task against 'task_routes[].id'. If none fits, use 'unknown_task_fallback'.
2. Read every document in the route's 'required_context' (resolve each 'ref' against 'entries[].id').
3. Read 'optional_context' only if the required context does not answer the task.
4. Check 'validation' before claiming the task is done.
5. Do not touch anything listed in 'do_not_modify_casually' without the process that entry names.
Optional helper: 'python scripts/python/agent_context.py route <task_class_id>' emits this same routing as JSON without hand-parsing this file.

machine_interfaces.invoke: read docs/agent/context-map.json directly, or use agent-context-helper

Validates committed reproducibility manifests against bound files.

Validates docs/findings/index.json, this context map, and the agent entry points for structural drift (dangling references, asymmetric supersession, unindexed documents, generated-artifact/role mismatches). One JSON document to stdout; nonzero exit on failure. See validate-agent-context-readme.

validation_commands.when: Any change under src/, including segmentation, normalization, rules, audit, or database logic.
Any change to src/segment.rs; refresh the affected measurements in docs/current-state.md rather than leaving them stale.
Any change under scripts/python/ that has a matching test_*.py file (run from the repository root).
Any change touching docs/manifests/ or the data it binds.

Any change to docs/findings/index.json, docs/agent/context-map.json, a docs/findings|gates|protocol document, or an agent entry-point file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, docs/agent/agent-contract.md).

task_routes.description: A fresh agent needs to understand what this repository is and what to do first, with no task-specific angle yet.
Updating docs/current-state.md, adding/editing a findings/gates/protocol document, or otherwise closing out a task's required handoff.

do_not_modify_casually.reason: Every findings/gates/protocol add or edit must also update its index entry (id, path, scope, status, summary, supersedes/superseded_by); do not let the index drift from the documents it catalogs.

task_routes.description: Changing segment_text/segment_line/build_unit/classify_kind/normalize_text or otherwise changing how Oracle text is split into units or normalized into templates.

do_not_modify_casually.reason: Frozen per-set exports and annotations are evidence artifacts; a segmenter/normalizer change can make them stale (drift) and requires the protocol's re-export/re-measure process, not a silent edit.
Corpus-wide baseline numbers in the verified data snapshot must be refreshed from a real run, never hand-edited.

task_routes.description: Running or continuing a per-set structural audit (preregistration, annotation passes, adjudication) under the frozen protocol.

do_not_modify_casually.reason: Frozen exports/annotations for a closed or in-progress audit are the audit's evidence; changing them outside the protocol's preregistration/adjudication steps invalidates the audit.
Frozen v1.0; changing it mid-audit changes the procedure the current audit was preregistered under.

task_routes.description: Changing how Scryfall bulk data is fetched, loaded, or shaped into cards.sqlite (scripts/python/mtg_card_pipeline.py and related database schema).

do_not_modify_casually.reason: Generated local artifact; regenerate, do not hand-edit or commit.
Committed manifests bind exact byte identities; a data-shape change requires a new manifest, not editing an existing one's recorded hashes.

task_routes.description: A question about game rules, rule citations, or how the rules parser exposes numbered rules and glossary entries.

do_not_modify_casually.reason: Tracked source data reflecting an official rules text snapshot; edits should be a deliberate snapshot update, not incidental text changes.

task_routes.description: Changing mtg-discover CLI commands, arguments, or output shape (src/main.rs, src/cli.rs) without changing segmentation/normalization semantics.

do_not_modify_casually.reason: Owns the held-out-pool exclusion at the query boundary; a CLI change that adds a new query path must preserve that exclusion, not bypass it.

task_routes.description: Proposing or evaluating a change to the frozen structural-investigation protocol/annotation guide, or preparing/reviewing a roadmap gate evidence package.

do_not_modify_casually.reason: Gate criteria and phase authorization are the program's scope-control mechanism (roadmap Section 2.3); changes need a written change record, not an inline edit.
Frozen v1.0; a protocol revision needs its own versioning and re-freeze, not a silent edit.

task_routes.description: Reviewing or adding external literature, existing-engine comparisons, or architecture references that inform (but do not decide) future IR/engine choices.
Any work toward a semantic IR, parser-beyond-segmentation, effect executor, or simulation. Not authorized by default; route to state and let it decide authorization, do not assume architecture.

do_not_modify_casually.reason: This task class is phase-gated; roadmap.md's gate criteria and deferred-work register determine what is currently authorized, not this file.

task_routes.note: This route intentionally names no architecture, IR, or design. It exists only to point an agent at the documents that govern whether and how such work may begin.

unknown_task_fallback.description: No task_routes entry matched. This is a conservative default, not a guess at intent: read the canonical entry documents, then ask for clarification or narrow the task before making changes.
